mentl/e251082:
§5.U's stride carrier reaches its first wide element. A [Float] is now a
first-class packed sequence end to end, and the same landing kills the
float-evidence-ft class.

The keystone is the word protocol: a handle IS a word, so the generic and
indirect-call boundary speaks word-arity only. A wide value (f64, stride 8)
crosses by reference, its address its word face — emit_wide_ref spills it to
a fresh cell and leaves the address, emit_wide_deref cashes it back, and
call_ft_name is always $ft{arity}. A wide-signatured fn (named, or a
capturing lambda) reaches the fn table through a $wf$<name> word-face wrapper
that derefs its args, direct-calls the native body at full speed, and spills
the wide result, so a polymorphic call site never needs the callee's
emission. The per-site repr-vector $ft — unsound at polymorphic sites — is
deleted.

The literal is born stride-8 (make_list_sc, the allocator's second face
paired with make_list). load_strided's wide arm returns the element address;
store_strided mem_copies stride bytes from the reference. Structural == over
[Float] compares values through list_eq_f64 (the word list_eq would
pointer-compare the references), with list_compare_f64 / list_hash_f64 /
float_to_str the ordering, hash and show leaves.

Reachability now contributes the f64 leaf family at the exact ==, ordering,
show and hash sites emit mints them: reach_names_expr gains wide_binop_seed
and wide_call_seed, reading each operand's live type through ty_has_wide_seq.
This is the visitor-walk projection the runtime-contract comment names, so a
float-free module drags in nothing; the reach index's declared row widens
honestly to LookupTy + EnvRead. make_list_sc joins the static contract as
make_list's paired second face.

One emit bug fixed en route: emit_wide_ref used $state_tmp for its spill
cell, clobbering the closure record a capturing lambda holds live there — the
k-cell was then read as a fn record, trapping indirect call type mismatch. A
dedicated $wide_cel

mentl/e21399c:
- Demotes "fold(map(...)) returns wrong value" from active blocker to
  fixed in fedb430. The root cause was in the capture detector, not
  in handler state leakage as initially hypothesized — filter_real_
  captures was filtering names matching top_globals without accounting
  for lexical shadowing, so inner fns inside a fn whose parameter
  matched a top-level name ended up reading the global instead of
  capturing the parameter. A single user `let xs = [1,2,3]` was enough
  to turn every collection-primitive into silent nonsense.

- Records the parallel follow-up bug (inner let shadowing top-level
  let) that the fix doesn't yet handle, along with three potential
  approaches for next session.

- Notes the lower_print.lux capture-visualization improvement as part
  of the fix commit — `tools/probe.sh lower` now shows closure
  captures per function, making this class of bug visible in a single
  glance instead of requiring WAT inspection.

The stage-2 self-compile remains blocked on the separate multi-line
lex/parse bug (issue #1 in the handoff), which is unrelated to
shadowing and needs its own investigation.

two-top/e2f99f8:
GAME_DESIGN_AUDIT read the match from the source. This reads the product
from the seat: seven personas, each with a different reason to pick the
phone up, each traced through the shipped code with a file and a line
behind every claim. 54 findings (16 red, 25 orange, 13 yellow), ~45
distinct once the seats' overlaps merge.

Nearly every one is one of two shapes. A failure the player is never
told about: signaling dies at ~6 s and the overlay is replaced by
nothing, forever; the join deep-link no-ops whenever the app is already
running; DesyncDetected is a tracing::error! and nothing else. Or a
number two phones don't agree on: a network drop makes BOTH phones
record a win for the same match, and a 2 s thermal hitch convicts you of
walking out. The rivalry ledger, the streaks, the signed results all
rest on both phones telling the same story, and they don't.

The pattern worth leading with is that this repo usually already
contains the fix, applied somewhere else, with a comment explaining why.
read_profile quarantines a corrupt file; load_career silently returns a
default and then overwrites the evidence. The theater refuses a
foreign-version tape on screen because "the no-migrations law should
read as a law, not as data loss"; RIVALS logs it and does nothing. The
recorder waits 30 frames for predicted ticks to settle; the ledger and
the attestation both commit on the predicted edge. SpawnGuard promises
it "can never be an offensive shield"; taunting doesn't break it, so
every death buys a free unpunishable taunt worth a third of the streak
ladder. Most of this list is three lines away in a neighbouring module.

Two structural ones that aren't: there is no lifecycle handling anywhere
in 13 crates, so a phone call past 9 s is an unrecoverable forfeit and
Android's scheduled dark theme at sunset re-enters android_main and
panics on subscriber re-registration. And the rollback session takes
ggrs's default 8-frame prediction window against a 9-frame cellular RTT
-- one f

stoop/e2572e8:
The Stage 0 app shipped with a photo tag that could not hold a photo, a
zine press that lost the issue on reload, an imposition that disagreed
with the hand kit in press/, and an author filter that matched nothing.
This makes the app the thing its own views promised.

Photos are real. Intake dithers to 1-bit with Floyd-Steinberg, per the
rule DESIGN.md already stated: a page-sized photo lands around 36 KB,
stays on the device, and arrives in the only form a photocopier can
honestly reproduce. Blobs live in IndexedDB because localStorage caps
out near 5 MB; state holds ids and sweeps orphans when entries go.

The press now agrees with press/. Its imposition is presetA, the same
one the hand kit uses, and check.sh fails the build if the two ever
diverge again; restoring the old layout trips it. Panels persist as
typed, the numbered test sheet and the fold swap come across from the
kit, and photos drop into panels from a tray. Compile pulls the log,
journal, lists and projects into the issue and puts the newest photo on
the cover.

Sync is a file that merges. Export carries photos; import unions by id
and prefers the newer copy, so two people can each export, swap, and end
up agreeing instead of clobbering each other. Replace stays available
and asks first. Entries now store an author key and an epoch stamp
rather than a display name and a formatted string, so renaming either
person leaves every past note attached to them, and the filter that
matched nothing matches.

app.js passed the 300-line ceiling, so it splits into src/js parts that
build.sh concatenates inside one IIFE: parts on disk, one function at
rest. rooms.css is renamed forms.css for what it now holds, dead skin
and defs markup is dropped, and README, CONTRIBUTING, DESIGN and SPEC
are corrected to describe the app that exists rather than the prototype
deleted in the previous commit.
